grounding.states: large eggs dropped into boiling water: 12 minutes gives a fully hard-boiled egg
grounding.from: Healthline says 12 to 13 minutes gives fully hard-boiled eggs that are not over-cooked

grounding.states: large eggs dropped into boiling water: 10 minutes is mostly cooked but slightly soft in the center
grounding.from: At 10 minutes, the eggs are mostly cooked through but slightly soft in the center

grounding.states: large eggs: past about 14-15 minutes the eggs turn rubbery or dry
grounding.from: Past about 14–15 minutes the eggs turn rubbery or dry

grounding.states: times are for large eggs; smaller eggs cook quicker, larger ones need more time
grounding.from: Healthline says these times are for large eggs: smaller ones cook quicker while larger ones need extra time

value.answer: For large eggs dropped into boiling water, 12 minutes gets you a fully set yolk. 10 is firm but a bit soft in the middle, and past about 14-15 they go rubbery and dry. Smaller eggs need a little less time, bigger ones a little more.
